questions.question: What is a sample space $S$ for a random experiment?
options: The set of all possible outcomes in the chosen model
A single outcome that actually occurs
The probability assigned to one event
A rule for averaging numerical outcomes, for every possible choice of input.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the role of the sample space?
options: It is the universe of possible results in the model
It lists only the outcomes with positive probability
It is always the set of real numbers
It is the event that is most likely to occur

questions.question: How are events related to the sample space?
options: Events are numbers outside the sample space
Events replace the sample space once probabilities are assigned
Events must contain every outcome in the sample space
Events are subsets of the sample space

questions.question: Why does the choice of sample space matter?
options: It forces every event to have probability one
It removes the need to define outcomes
It fixes which results and events can be discussed
It makes all real situations have the same model

questions.question: For a random experiment, what must the sample space include?
options: Only the most common outcome
Only impossible outcomes
Only outcomes with numerical values
Every possible outcome in the model

questions.question: For one coin toss modeled by its face, which sample space is appropriate?
options: $S=\{HH,HT,TH,TT\}$
$S=[0,+\infty)$

questions.question: For one roll of a standard die, which set is a natural sample space?
For two dice where the order of the dice is recorded, which sample space matches the model?
For a waiting-time experiment measured in minutes, which sample space is natural?
If $S=\{HH,HT,TH,TT\}$ for two coin tosses, which object is an outcome in $S$?
options: $HT$
$S^c$
$P(HH)$

questions.question: Why can the same real situation have different sample spaces?
options: The sample space is chosen after probabilities are calculated
Different models may record different levels of detail
A sample space cannot contain nonnumerical outcomes
Every experiment has exactly one mathematically possible sample space

questions.question: What goes wrong if a possible outcome is left out of the sample space $S$?
options: All events automatically become disjoint
The sample space becomes a random variable, which is not the issue here
Some probabilities refer to results outside the model
The complement rule becomes $P(A^c)=P(A)$

questions.question: If $S$ is changed from ordered dice pairs to dice sums, what changes most directly?
options: The physical dice being rolled
The requirement that events are subsets of $S$
The fact that probabilities must be nonnegative
The outcomes of the model

questions.question: A coin is tossed twice. If only the number of heads is recorded, which sample space fits that model?
options: $\{HH,HT,TH,TT\}$

questions.question: A coin is tossed twice. If the order of heads and tails is recorded, which sample space fits that model?
options: $\{HH,HT,TH,TT\}$

questions.question: Let $S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}$ for one die roll. Which set is an event in this model?
For two coin tosses, one model records order and another records head count. How do $\{HH,HT,TH,TT\}$ and $\{0,1,2\}$ compare?
options: They are the same sample space written with different symbols
The first is an event and the second is a probability function
The second is invalid because sample spaces cannot contain numbers
They are two different sample spaces for different recorded information

questions.question: Why is $S=\{2,4,6\}$ not a sample space for the experiment 'roll one die and record the face'?
options: It contains too many outcomes for one die roll
It is an event rather than a valid subset
It assigns probabilities before outcomes are defined
It omits possible modeled outcomes such as $1$, $3$, and $5$

questions.question: A customer order is modeled by item type and delivery time. Which candidate is a single outcome, not a sample space?
options: all possible item-time pairs
the set of all delivery times
(book, 2 days)
the event 'delivery within 3 days'

questions.question: Suppose an experiment records a nonnegative waiting time $T$. Which event is properly expressed as a subset of the sample space $S=[0,+\infty)$?
options: $P(T\le 5)$
